title: What Unilever shares with Google and Apple
summary: Unilever, a consumer-products giant, comes in at No. 3 on LinkedIn's list of most sought-after employers, just behind Google and Apple. CEO Paul Polman attributes this success to Unilever's strong sense of purpose, which attracts talent, especially Millennials, and drives the company's core strategy to positively impact the environment and public health. This purpose-driven approach, despite challenges from short-term investor pressures, has led to increased job applications, improved employee engagement, and ambitious sustainability goals.

title: Thomas Kurian is new Oracle president
summary: Oracle Corporation has promoted Thomas Kurian, executive vice-president of product development, to the role of president. This appointment follows Larry Ellison's move to executive chairman and the leadership transition to Safra Catz and Mark Hurd. Kurian, responsible for Oracle's software product portfolio, has significantly grown the software division's annual sales under his leadership.

title: What Microsoft is buying with its $7.2 billion Nokia purchase
summary: Microsoft announced its plan to acquire Nokia's handset and services business for $7.2 billion, aiming to strengthen its position in the mobile market. This move allows Microsoft to control the hardware for its Windows Phone operating system, similar to Apple's strategy, and potentially brings Stephen Elop back into a leadership role within the company. The acquisition is seen as a strategic bet for Microsoft to gain relevance in the mobile age, despite skepticism regarding its potential impact on market share.

title: Renew blue: Best Buy’s turnaround strategy
summary: Best Buy launched its "renew blue" strategy in 2012 to improve its financial position by strengthening vendor relationships, revamping stores, increasing same-store sales, and growing its online business. This strategy has already generated significant cost reductions and involves unique partnerships with suppliers like Samsung and Microsoft to create "stores-within-a-store." The company continues to focus on cost reduction, online sales expansion, and improving store traffic as part of its ongoing turnaround efforts.

title: Can IBM CEO Ginni Rometty Survive?
summary: This article questions the future of IBM CEO Ginni Rometty as the company continues to struggle, particularly in the cloud computing market where it lags behind competitors. IBM's board faces a difficult decision regarding her leadership following disappointing financial performance and a negative 2015 earnings guidance. The author suggests that being late to market in a critical sector like cloud computing, without unique features, makes a turnaround difficult for IBM under current leadership.

title: Starbucks Names Kevin Johnson President and Chief Operating Officer
summary: Starbucks Corporation announced the appointment of Kevin Johnson as president and chief operating officer, effective March 1, 2015. Johnson, a Starbucks board member since 2009 and former CEO of Juniper Networks and president of Microsoft's Platforms Division, will lead the company's global operating businesses and key technology platforms. He will report to Howard Schultz and will oversee the transition from current COO Troy Alstead, who is taking a sabbatical.

title: CloudOn app to shut down after Dropbox acquisition
summary: Dropbox has acquired CloudOn Inc., an Israel-based startup, and plans to shut down its product offering while absorbing its team. This move follows a partnership between Dropbox and Microsoft to enable mobile editing of Office documents directly in Dropbox, and CloudOn's collaboration tool, which previously offered an Office alternative, faces reduced market viability due to Microsoft's native iOS Office applications. The CloudOn app will discontinue service on March 15 and is no longer accepting new customers.

title: Investing in Quantum Computing with TINY and D-Wave
summary: This article discusses investing in quantum computing through Harris and Harris Group (NASDAQ:TINY) and its investment in D-Wave Systems. It explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize problem-solving and details D-Wave's technology, investors, and valuation. The piece also considers potential competitors like IBM and critiques surrounding D-Wave's claims, advising investors on how to gain exposure to D-Wave's potential.

title: Ray Dalio's Bridgewater picks up chunk of Microsoft, ditches UPS
summary: Ray Dalio's Bridgewater Associates significantly increased its stake in Microsoft Corp. while divesting its holdings in SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust and United Parcel Service Inc. during the last quarter. The hedge fund, despite seeing its equity holdings decline in value, still outperformed most peers in January with an 8.3% gain, managing $160 billion in assets. These portfolio changes were detailed in a recent SEC filing.

title: 4 IBM Blunders That Gave Big Blue's Competition the Edge (NYSE: IBM)
summary: This article details four significant blunders made by IBM that allowed its competitors, such as Apple, Microsoft, Intel, and HP, to gain a competitive edge in various technology markets. These missteps include abandoning the first smartphone (Simon), ceding control of operating systems to Microsoft, failing to capitalize on microprocessor development, and dismissing the low-margin laser printer market. The author suggests that these strategic errors have contributed to IBM's struggles compared to its more successful tech industry peers.

title: Indian tech giant Infosys buys Israeli firm for $200m
summary: Indian tech services firm Infosys announced the acquisition of Israeli cloud tech firm Panaya for $200 million. This deal is considered one of the largest tech acquisitions between India and Israel and aims to enhance Infosys's services for customers using databases like SAP and Oracle. The acquisition highlights increasing interest from Indian companies in Israel's information technology sector, further strengthening business ties between the two nations.

title: How SailPoint Technologies is reinventing identity management
summary: SailPoint Technologies, founded by Mark McClain, specializes in identity and access management software, addressing the persistent challenges in this crowded space by focusing on customer service and adapting to new technologies like cloud-based identity solutions. The company differentiates itself from larger competitors through its agility and commitment to strong company culture, which emphasizes Innovation, Integrity, Impact, and Individuals, while also pursuing ambitious growth goals including a potential IPO.

title: Insights about the changes in Lumia 635 – Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) in Focus
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced that the Lumia 635 with 16GB of RAM will be among the first phones to launch with Windows 10, addressing customer demand for better storage and multitasking capabilities. This upgrade will allow for playing games in high quality and improved multitasking, though it will mean a compromise on battery life. The company is also expected to make further announcements regarding 512MB phones and Windows 10 compatibility at the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona in 2015.

title: Microsoft rolls out MSN apps suite for iOS & Android
summary: Microsoft has rolled out a suite of MSN apps for iOS and Android devices, expanding its reach beyond Windows platforms. These free apps, including MSN News, Health and Fitness, Money, Sports, Food and Drink, and Weather, allow users to access their personalized preferences across different devices. This move aims to connect with non-Windows Mobile OS users and integrate Microsoft experiences across various platforms.

title: Five KC area billionaires on Forbes’ list
summary: Forbes' 2015 list of the world's billionaires includes five individuals from the Kansas City area, with Min Kao of Garmin leading the local contingent. Bill Gates maintained his position as the world's richest person, with his net worth increasing to $79.2 billion. The list saw a rise in the total number of billionaires this year, reaching 1,826.

title: Alibaba investment puts Snapchat valuation at $15 billion
summary: Snapchat Inc. secured a $200-million investment from Chinese technology giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., reportedly valuing the company at $15 billion. This investment validates Snapchat's unique social media features and its rapid growth into a significant force in media and advertising, despite facing operational challenges and criticism for turning down a $3 billion Facebook acquisition offer. The partnership also hints at potential future revenue streams for Snapchat through e-commerce integration, as Alibaba seeks to expand its U.S. presence.

title: BlackBerry Ltd (BBRY) Uses International Business Machines Corp. (IBM)’s Software in its Tablet Computer
summary: BlackBerry Ltd's Secusmart unit has launched the SecuTABLET, a tablet computer that utilizes International Business Machines Corp. (IBM)’s software within a Samsung-based tablet. This device is designed for government and corporate users, allowing access to consumer applications while maintaining the security of confidential work-related data, addressing the need to separate personal and professional digital lives. The SecuTABLET employs a small chip-card for encryption and IBM software to protect applications within a virtual container, aimed at preventing data corruption by malware.

title: Hancock Tower seeking high-tech tenants
summary: Boston Properties is attempting to reposition the lower floors of the iconic John Hancock Tower to attract high-tech tenants, offering a separate entrance, fresher vibe, and larger, more efficient floor plans. This move responds to the booming Greater Boston tech scene, with companies seeking urban locations and more affordable rents than those found in Kendall Square or the tower's upper floors. The rebranded "120 St. James" space aims to cater to firms that prioritize value and efficiency over towering views, even potentially using the former observation deck entrance.

title: T-Mobile turns its focus to small businesses with new offers
summary: T-Mobile is launching new "Un-carrier for Business" plans focused on simplicity and affordability to attract small businesses, two years after revolutionizing consumer wireless services. The new offerings include simplified rate structures, incentives for switching, and discounts for employees' family plans, aiming to compete with larger carriers like Verizon and AT&T. T-Mobile also introduces benefits like free domain names and Microsoft Office 365 tools for businesses purchasing extra data.

title: Cyanogen Raises $80 Million With Backing From Twitter, Telefonica and Rupert Murdoch
summary: Cyanogen, an open Android startup, has closed an $80 million Series C funding round with investments from notable strategic partners including Twitter Ventures, Qualcomm Incorporated, Telefónica Ventures, Smartfren Telecom, and Rupert Murdoch, led by Premji Invest. This funding aims to boost Cyanogen's technical and marketing capabilities as it seeks to offer a legitimate alternative to Google's Android services. The company's goal is to become the third leading mobile OS by empowering the mobile ecosystem with an open computing platform.

title: Microsoft Corporation (MSFT)’s Apps Get Pre-installed in Certain Google Inc (GOOGL)’s Android based Samsung Tablets
summary: Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) announced that its apps, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Skype, OneNote, and OneDrive, will be pre-installed on certain Android-based Samsung tablets set to launch this year. This expands a previous agreement for Samsung's Galaxy S6 handsets and reflects Microsoft's strategy to make its cloud-enabled software available across different platforms, including those by Google Inc (GOOGL) and Apple Inc. (AAPL), to reach a broader user base. Users will have free access to basic features of these apps, with premium features requiring payment.

title: Google hires new CFO: Morgan Stanley's Ruth Porat, 'the most powerful woman on Wall Street'
summary: Google has announced Ruth Porat, Morgan Stanley's CFO, will be joining the company as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective May 26. Porat, described as "the most powerful woman on Wall Street," will be returning to California, replacing the retiring Patrick Pichette. Google CEO Larry Page expressed enthusiasm for Porat's experience and contributions to the company's innovation and investments.

title: Former HP and Oracle man K. Raman takes over at Microsoft Malaysia
summary: K. Raman, a veteran with 25 years of IT industry experience including 15 years at HP and a regional leadership role at Oracle, has been appointed as the new managing director of Microsoft Malaysia. His appointment comes during a period of significant transformation for Microsoft, which is focused on becoming a 'Productivity and Platform' company for a mobile- and cloud-first world. Raman aims to leverage Microsoft's platform and partnerships to support Malaysia's national development goals.

title: Measuring product-development vitality
summary: The article discusses the "Vitality Index," a key corporate R&D performance metric that measures the percentage of total company sales from new products. It explores the challenges in defining "new product" and its lifespan, highlighting the varied approaches companies take. The author also provides benchmarks for different levels of vitality and the impact of the chosen "N" value (length of time a product is considered new) on reported figures and corporate strategy.

title: Sunny Days: Hyatt Credits OpenText Cloud for 'World Class' Intranet
summary: Hyatt Hotels has dramatically improved its intranet, "Hyatt Connect," leading to a 500 percent increase in use among its 75,000 employees over five years. The Chicago-based hotel chain credits OpenText's cloud infrastructure for providing a cost-effective, scalable, and supportive solution that offers 24/7 support and helps manage content and applications. This move shifted Hyatt from a basic internal portal to a "world-class" intranet that facilitates communication and operations for its global workforce.

title: Lessons for Expedia: What it’s like to move an entire company to Seattle from the Eastside
summary: This article discusses the potential move of Expedia's headquarters from Bellevue to Seattle, examining the challenges and benefits based on Glympse's similar experience. Key considerations include employee commute times, parking, recruiting advantages, and proximity to the region's tech hub. While a longer commute is a drawback, Glympse's CEO highlights improved recruiting from Seattle and being closer to the innovation "center of gravity" as significant upsides.

title: Rovi, AT&T and Microsoft have largest video on-demand patent portfolios
summary: This article examines the companies with the largest patent portfolios in the video on-demand (VOD) sector, identifying Rovi, AT&T, and Microsoft as the leaders. It delves into specific patents held by these companies, showcasing their innovations in VOD technologies like content identification, recommendations, and efficient content delivery. The article also highlights how these companies leverage their patent holdings for licensing and competitive advantage in the burgeoning VOD market.

title: Google, Apple and Microsoft defend tax set-up that shifts revenue offshore
summary: Senior executives from Google, Apple, and Microsoft defended their corporate structures before a Senate inquiry, explaining that revenue from Australian operations is often taxed in offshore jurisdictions due to the global tax system. News Corp Australia also appeared, advocating for a GST on Netflix, which competes with its own streaming service. The article highlights the ongoing debate about multinational corporate tax avoidance and potential "Google taxes" to address profit shifting.

title: First look: Microsoft Lumia 640 and Lumia 640 XL
summary: Microsoft Devices has launched the Lumia 640 and Lumia 640 XL smartphones in India. Both devices run Windows Phone 8.1 with Lumia Denim and are upgradable to Windows 10. The Lumia 640 XL features a 5.7-inch HD display and a 13MP ZEISS optics camera, while the Lumia 640 has a 5-inch screen and an 8MP rear camera.

title: Surface 3 Now Available in Malaysia
summary: The Surface 3 is now available for pre-order in Malaysia starting April 13, 2015, with retail availability planned for May 5, 2015. Positioned as a tablet that can replace a laptop, it offers an affordable and lightweight design, optimized for full Windows and Office with long battery life. The device comes in 64GB and 128GB versions, with pricing starting from RM1,989, and includes a one-year subscription to Microsoft Office 365 Personal.

title: Moroccan Aziz Benmalek Appointed Vice-President at Microsoft’s WWHCS
summary: Moroccan Aziz Benmalek has been appointed Vice-President of Worldwide Hosting & Cloud Services at Microsoft Corporation. In this role, he will oversee the WW Hosting & Cloud Services business for the U.S. market and lead strategy and go-to-market efforts for hosting and managed services providers. Benmalek brings 24 years of experience in the technology industry, with 18 years at Microsoft, and holds degrees from École Centrale Paris and the European School of Management.

title: City Council Speaker Strikes Deal to Provide Microsoft Software to CUNY Students
summary: City Council Speaker Melissa Mark-Viverito, Microsoft Corporation, and The City University of New York announced a collaboration to provide free Microsoft Office 365 to over 400,000 CUNY students. This public-private partnership aims to expand access to tech education and prepare students for the global workforce. Students can download Office 365 on multiple devices at no cost, gaining access to the latest applications and cloud storage.
source: The City University of New York

title: Sony Hackers Used Phishing Emails to Breach Company Networks
summary: A security researcher revealed that phishing emails were used to breach Sony Picture Entertainment's computer networks. Hackers leveraged fake Apple ID verification emails to obtain credentials, then used them in conjunction with LinkedIn profiles to access Sony network login information. Recommendations include memory process injection protection, user credential monitoring, and avoiding password reuse to prevent similar attacks.

title: Business | Rhode Island’s Hasbro Ranked 2nd Best Corporate Citizen in U.S.
summary: Hasbro Inc. has been ranked second overall on Corporate Responsibility Magazine's 100 Best Corporate Citizens of 2015, coming in behind Microsoft Corporation. The Pawtucket-based toy manufacturer received strong rankings in human rights, philanthropy, environment, and employee relations, though its financial and corporate governance rankings were lower. The article also includes several other rankings for Rhode Island in various categories such as insurance premiums, eco-friendliness, and business climate.

title: Apple Inc. (AAPL), Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), Google Inc (GOOGL) & Microsoft Corporation (MSFT): 4 Horsemen Of NASDAQ
summary: This article discusses the performance of four major tech companies—Apple, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft—dubbed the "4 Horsemen of NASDAQ," in early 2015. Amazon showed the most significant growth with over 45% YTD, followed by Apple and Google, while Microsoft had more modest gains. Analysts James Cakmak and Jason Helfstein weighed in on Amazon's impressive turnaround, particularly highlighting its web services business.

title: Number of Mobile-Only Internet Users Now Exceeds Desktop-Only in the U.S.
summary: For the first time in March 2015, the number of mobile-only adult internet users in the U.S. exceeded desktop-only users. While a large majority of the digital population is multi-platform, this milestone signifies the smartphone's rise as the primary internet access point. Desktops still remain important for complex tasks and online retail purchases, but the trend points towards a "mobile first" evolution of digital media.

title: Whitney George: You want to find "sick" companies that are going to get better
summary: Value investor Whitney George, recently joined Sprott Asset Management, discusses his investment philosophy focusing on identifying financially strong companies experiencing temporary setbacks. He emphasizes the importance of good management and strong corporate governance, particularly in owner-operated businesses, and explains his rationale for investing in asset managers and maintaining a diversified portfolio including hard assets like precious metals as a hedge against financial instability. George also touches on the current market environment skewed by zero-interest rates and the opportunities he sees in the mining sector despite its recent underperformance.

title: Oracle Emerges As Favorite For Estimated $50B Salesforce Takeover
summary: Investors are speculating that Salesforce.com could be acquired, with Oracle Corp. emerging as the leading candidate for a potential $50 billion takeover. This deal would reunite Oracle Chairman Larry Ellison and Salesforce.com CEO Marc Benioff, both prominent figures in Silicon Valley, and represents Oracle's push to strengthen its position in cloud computing. Analysts view Oracle as the most logical buyer due to its financial capacity and strategic need to expand its cloud services against rivals like Salesforce.

title: Erik Huggers, ex-iPlayer exec, confirmed as Vevo CEO
summary: Vevo has appointed Erik Huggers, formerly of Intel and the BBC, as its new President and Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. Huggers brings a strong background in digital media and streaming services, having launched BBC iPlayer and led Intel's media division. His appointment is expected to drive innovation and growth for the music video platform, which currently delivers nearly 100 billion streams annually.

title: Oracle co-CEO Safra Catz stifles Salesforce acquisition rumor
summary: Oracle co-CEO Safra Catz has downplayed rumors of Oracle acquiring Salesforce, suggesting that any acquisition of Salesforce by another company could actually benefit Oracle by creating market disruption. While Oracle aims to be a leader in cloud computing and acquiring Salesforce would accelerate this goal, Catz highlighted the challenges of large tech mergers and the significant cultural differences between Oracle and Salesforce. Analysts suggest that if Oracle stays out, potential buyers for Salesforce could include SAP, Microsoft, IBM, and Hewlett-Packard.

title: Teens & Older Demos Driving Gains in U.S. Smartphone Penetration...
summary: U.S. smartphone penetration reached 77% in March, with teens and older age groups showing the fastest growth. Notably, teens aged 13-17, 45-54 year olds, and those 65+ each saw double-digit percentage point increases in penetration. The article suggests that smartphones are now viewed as mainstream rather than a luxury, driving adoption across all demographics.

title: Microsoft Philippines seals partnership with Solar Entertainment Corporation
summary: Microsoft Philippines has partnered with Solar Entertainment Corporation (SEC) through an enterprise agreement to enhance productivity and communication within the media organization. SEC will deploy Office 365, Microsoft’s cloud-based productivity suite, to address challenges arising from its expanding, mobile, and collaborative workforce. This deployment aims to leverage cloud innovation to improve how SEC employees work in the digital age.

title: Amazon says its cloud not bitten by Venom flaw
summary: Amazon stated that its cloud services were not affected by the "Venom" bug (CVE-2015-3456), which impacts various virtualized platforms including QEMU, Xen, and KVM. Other companies like Rackspace and Red Hat issued advisories and patches, with Rackspace requiring customers to reboot virtual machines. The vulnerability differs from a previous Xen-specific bug in its wider potential impact due to the ubiquity of affected hypervisors within data centers and cloud infrastructures.

title: Microsoft study claims human attention span now lags behind goldfish
summary: A Microsoft study conducted in Canada claims that the average human attention span has decreased to eight seconds, one second shorter than that of a goldfish, down from twelve seconds in 2000. While digital devices may improve multi-tasking and the ability to filter desired information, heavy users may struggle to focus when required, and multi-screen users face difficulty filtering information. Researchers suggest this shorter attention span could be a normal adaptation to new technology.

title: Human attention span down to just eight seconds
summary: A Microsoft study revealed that the human attention span has decreased to just eight seconds, a drop from 12 seconds in 2000. This is now less than that of a goldfish, and the study attributes this decline to the rise in digital technology. While attention spans have shortened, the ability to multitask has improved.

title: HKSTP & Microsoft Hong Kong Kick Off City’s Transformation Into Internet of Things (IoT) Hub
summary: HKSTP and Microsoft Hong Kong announced a partnership to transform Hong Kong into an Internet of Things (IoT) hub in Asia. This collaboration involves a Memorandum of Understanding injecting over one million US Dollars to develop the IoT industry through an "IoT Innovation Platform," the first of its kind in Asia. The initiative aims to support IoT developers, including students, startups, and software vendors, by providing resources, cloud services, and expert advice to accelerate their solution development.

title: Charter agrees to buy Time Warner Cable for $56 billion
summary: Charter Communications Inc. has agreed to acquire Time Warner Cable Inc. for $56 billion, aiming to consolidate the second and third largest US cable operators to better compete with Comcast Corp. The cash-and-stock deal values Time Warner Cable at $78.7 billion including debt, and will create a new public company called New Charter. This acquisition follows a rejected bid by Charter and a failed $45 billion offer from Comcast due to regulatory concerns.

title: Microsoft To Boost Support For Armenian IT Sector
summary: Microsoft Corporation has pledged to enhance its contribution to Armenia's IT sector by establishing a new regional software development center in Yerevan. In return, the Armenian government committed to stronger protection against software piracy. This collaboration aims to boost Armenia's competitiveness in global hi-tech industries and attract further foreign investment.

title: NetApp rebrands Riverbed’s SteelStore as AltaVault
summary: NetApp has rebranded Riverbed’s SteelStore as AltaVault, a new cloud backup product range. This acquisition, made in October 2014 for $80 million, provides secure data backup to the cloud with advanced deduplication and compression. The AltaVault range includes physical, virtual, and cloud-based appliances, with a new flagship physical appliance, AVA800, expected later in 2015.

title: Business sets the digital pace at Rentokil Initial
summary: Rentokil Initial's digital transformation began with business departments leading initiatives like Google Apps adoption and mobile app development, bypassing traditional IT. This led enterprise IT to embrace a new strategy, "decomposing" its core ERP into an API infrastructure to support rapid innovation and new capabilities like IoT applications. The shift highlights how business-led IT initiatives can accelerate technological change and the replacement of legacy systems within an organization.

title: NetEase's Fantasy Westward Journey reaches #4 in App Annie's worldwide iOS revenue chart
summary: NetEase's mobile game, Fantasy Westward Journey, achieved the #4 spot in App Annie's worldwide iOS revenue chart in April 2015, demonstrating the growing power of Chinese brands globally. This success follows the game's launch in March 2015, where it quickly dominated the China iOS App Store, and comes as NetEase expands its global presence, including a new US office and partnerships with companies like Blizzard Entertainment. The company also reported a 54.2% year-over-year revenue increase in Q1 2015, reflecting its strong commitment to quality.

title: The 10 Most Profitable Companies in the Fortune 500
summary: This article identifies the 10 most profitable companies in the Fortune 500 for 2014, highlighting their profits and key factors influencing their performance. Tech giants Apple and Microsoft, banks Wells Fargo and J.P. Morgan, and oil producers ExxonMobil and Chevron are prominent, with Apple leading in profits. The article details individual company performance, including financial figures and notable events from 2014.

title: AMD unveils project Quantum: Ultra-small PC with extreme performance
summary: AMD has unveiled Project Quantum, a small form-factor PC designed to deliver extreme gaming performance at 4K resolutions. This console-like system will feature an unknown multi-core AMD processor, two AMD Radeon R9 Fury "Fiji" GPUs with 8GB of HBM memory in CrossFireX, and liquid cooling. While pricing is expected to be premium and the exact manufacturing process is unclear, Quantum PCs are anticipated to ship with Microsoft Windows 10 and DirectX 12 this fall or holiday season.

title: Oracle eyes new competition as it pushes into the cloud
summary: Oracle is shifting its competitive focus from traditional tech giants like IBM to cloud-based rivals such as Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce (CRM), and Workday. Founder Larry Ellison unveiled over 24 new cloud products, emphasizing Oracle's comprehensive offerings compared to competitors. The company faces the challenge of establishing itself in a cloud market already dominated by long-standing players.

title: GE And GM: Old Companies Become A New Breed Of Software Companies
summary: General Electric and General Motors, traditionally manufacturing giants, are rapidly transforming into software companies to adapt to the digital age. Both companies are significantly increasing their IT workforces and investing heavily in software and analytics, recognizing that digital capabilities are crucial for future growth and innovation. This trend suggests a broader evolution where technology is expanding into every aspect of enterprises, making every modern corporation, to a large degree, an information technology company.

title: Facebook (Nasdaq: FB) Joins Top 10 Companies by Market Cap
summary: Facebook (Nasdaq: FB) has surpassed Wal-Mart Stores Inc. (NYSE: WMT) to join the top 10 companies by market capitalization, following a strong stock rally. This achievement highlights Facebook's rapid growth since its 2012 IPO, expanding its influence across tech, mobile, advertising, and virtual reality with acquisitions like Oculus. The article also details Facebook's strategic initiatives in mobile advertising and video to drive future growth.

title: SQL Big Data Services Highlight New Oracle Cloud Offerings
summary: Oracle has introduced new Big Data services within its Oracle Cloud Platform, including the Oracle Big Data Cloud Service and Big Data SQL Cloud Service. These offerings combine Apache Hadoop with SQL integration, aiming to provide familiar tools for enterprises to manage and analyze Big Data. Oracle also announced the Oracle Database Cloud - Exadata Service and Oracle Archive Storage Cloud Service, directly competing with Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services respectively.

title: Oracle plans to rival Amazon by extending cloud services
summary: Oracle Corp is expanding its cloud-computing offerings to directly compete with Amazon.com Inc, with founder Larry Ellison stating Oracle is prepared to compete on price. Oracle's new Oracle Cloud Platform, including an archive storage service, aims to provide a cost-effective alternative to Amazon Web Services and Amazon Glacier. The company's cloud business is growing rapidly, with $2.3 billion in annual revenue, though still trailing market leaders like Amazon and Microsoft.

title: Microsoft to nurture start-ups in pact with Mumbai institute
summary: Microsoft Corporation is partnering with the Indian School of Design and Innovation (ISDI) in Mumbai to incubate 12 new start-ups. This three-year partnership, formalized on Wednesday, will establish the ISDI Creative Accelerator, offering lab facilities, mentoring, and funding. The initiative aims to improve the quality of products from Indian start-ups by emphasizing design, recognizing India as the third-largest base for young businesses globally.

title: From megawatts to megabytes, coal-fired TVA power plant gets a makeover
summary: A former coal-fired power plant in north Alabama owned by the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) is being redeveloped into a data center for Google Inc. This transformation of the Widows Creek Fossil Plant signifies a shift from traditional energy production to powering internet services. The $600 million project, expected to begin construction in early 2016, will also involve TVA partnering with Google to secure clean energy resources, creating 100 new jobs and symbolizing a move towards a green energy economy.

title: Microsoft might be interested in buying AMD, according to source
summary: A source familiar with the matter indicates that Microsoft Corp. may acquire Advanced Micro Devices to revive its chip design operations. Microsoft has substantial cash reserves compared to AMD's market capitalization, making an acquisition relatively easy given AMD's current valuation is significantly lower than their purchase of ATI Technologies in 2006. Such a move could lead to considerable savings for Microsoft on components for its Xbox One and other hardware devices.

title: Microsoft MapPoint 2006
summary: Microsoft MapPoint 2006 is a software solution designed to visualize and analyze data geographically. It includes new features like GPS-based driving and updated demographic databases from 2004 and consumer behavior data from 2003. The software integrates with Microsoft Office and allows users to easily import their own data, create various map types, and plan business trips with turn-by-turn directions.

title: Kyocera, Microsoft Expand Technology Sharing Agreement - Source
summary: Kyocera Corporation and Microsoft Corp. have signed an agreement to expand their existing patent licensing arrangement, allowing them to use a broader range of each other's technologies. This agreement strengthens their partnership and resolves a previously filed patent infringement lawsuit. The specific details of the agreement remain confidential.

title: Gartner’s 2015 Cloud Storage Magic Quadrant: Our Key Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2015 Magic Quadrant for Public Cloud Storage Services highlights Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, and Google as market leaders, dominating smaller vendors like Verizon, Rackspace, IBM, and AT&T, which are relegated to niche markets. The report provides insights into the "hyperscale vendors'" strategies, including Google's aggressive pricing and Microsoft's strong infrastructure, while also noting criticisms such as AWS's complex pricing. It underscores the intense competition and evolving landscape of the cloud storage market.

title: Microsoft announces restructuring of phone hardware business
summary: Microsoft announced a significant restructuring of its phone hardware business, resulting in the reduction of up to 7,800 positions and an impairment charge of approximately $7.6 billion related to its Nokia Devices and Services acquisition. This move signals a shift from growing a standalone phone business to focusing on a broader Windows ecosystem, including first-party devices, with the aim of running a more effective and focused phone portfolio in the near-term. Further details regarding these charges will be provided in Microsoft's upcoming financial reports.

title: Microsoft cuts another 7,800 jobs, takes $7.6 billion “impairment charge”
summary: Microsoft announced another round of layoffs, cutting 7,800 positions primarily within its phone business, and will record a significant $7.6 billion impairment charge related to its acquisition of Nokia's devices and services business. This decision comes shortly after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hinted at difficult choices ahead, with the impairment reflecting that the future performance of Nokia is below original expectations. The company emphasized that these cuts are part of a strategy to refocus on its core businesses.

title: Microsoft to cut 7,800 more jobs; writes off $7.6 billion in Nokia deal
summary: Microsoft announced a major restructuring of its mobile devices business, writing off $7.6 billion from its Nokia acquisition and cutting 7,800 jobs globally, primarily in its phone segment. This marks the second round of significant job cuts under CEO Satya Nadella, as the company shifts its strategy from a standalone phone business to growing a vibrant Windows ecosystem. Microsoft aims to narrow its focus to three key customer segments and run a more effective, narrower phone portfolio.

title: Microsoft signs General Electric to big Office 365 deal, covering 300k employees
summary: General Electric has signed a major agreement with Microsoft to roll out Office 365 to over 300,000 employees across 170 countries. This deal marks a significant win for Microsoft in the cloud-based productivity market, especially given GE's previous use of Google Apps. The implementation will include Skype for Business, Yammer, and integration with third-party services like Box.

title: TripAdvisor hopes lavish new headquarters in Needham will boost hiring
summary: TripAdvisor has opened a lavish new 282,000-square-foot headquarters in Needham, designed with amenities like a fitness center, game room, and free lunches, hoping to attract top tech talent in a competitive market. The company currently has 100 open positions and designed the office to enable employees to be social and active, though recruiters have mixed opinions on how much office environment alone drives hiring. The town of Needham offered TripAdvisor $1.8 million in reduced taxes over 13 years to attract the company.

title: LG Display to invest one billion in flexible OLED panels
summary: LG Display announced a significant investment of KRW 1.05 trillion ($0.91 billion) into a new 6th generation flexible OLED display production line at its Gumi Plant in Korea. This investment aims to drastically increase production efficiency for flexible and foldable displays, helping LG meet growing demand in the mobile, automotive, and television markets and prevent supply shortages. Mass production is scheduled to begin in the first half of 2017, reinforcing LG's position in advanced display technologies.

title: If Microsoft made laptops, it'd make this: HP Spectre x360
summary: This article reviews the HP Spectre x360 laptop, highlighting its design as a collaborative effort between HP and Microsoft, and comparing it to what a Microsoft Surface laptop might be like. It details the machine's aesthetic, specs, and innovative hinge design, concluding that it offers a solid and stylish convertible experience.

title: HP buys Stackato to beef up cloud development
summary: Hewlett-Packard (HPQ) is acquiring Stackato, a platform-as-a-service product from its long-time partner ActiveState, to bolster its hybrid cloud strategy. This acquisition strengthens HP's Helion portfolio and commitment to open-source solutions amidst its ongoing corporate overhaul and struggles in the public cloud market. HP will position Stackato to boost its hybrid cloud worldview, which focuses on integrating on-premise systems with external cloud services.

title: Microsoft’s Cortana will come to iOS and Android phones with Windows 10
summary: Microsoft's voice assistant, Cortana, is expanding beyond Windows Phone and Windows 10 PCs to iOS and Android devices. This cross-platform move will be facilitated by a "Phone Companion" app bundled with Windows 10, allowing users to connect their mobile devices to their Windows PCs and download the Cortana app. Cortana will offer features like reminders, alarms, and flight tracking, with synchronized changes across all devices.

title: Windows 10 downloads available from July 29: New features you should know about
summary: Microsoft's new Windows 10 operating system was made available worldwide on July 29, 2015, as a free upgrade for users of Windows 7 and 8.1. The article highlights several new features including a revamped Start menu, the Continuum feature for cross-device integration, enhanced Cortana functionality, and universal apps for music and video. Microsoft also aimed to attract a billion new users by making it easier for Android and iOS apps to run on Windows 10.

title: Manufacturing 4.0: the Connected Enterprise
summary: This article discusses Rockwell Automation's "Connected Enterprise" vision within the context of Manufacturing 4.0. It highlights the shift towards open EtherNet standards, declining costs of network nodes, and the importance of bridging IT and Operational Technology. The piece also addresses immediate steps manufacturers can take, the role of data analysis, and challenges related to cybersecurity and workforce skills in adopting these new technologies.

title: Windows 10 Will Bring New Features Every 4 Months
summary: Gartner's Stephen Kleynhans advises organizations to prepare for continuous Windows 10 updates by setting up test groups and adapting to a new update model, with feature updates expected roughly every four months. He details the service branch models (current, CBB, long-term servicing) and provides guidance on hardware considerations and upgrading from older Windows versions. Kleynhans recommends IT pros "kick the tires" for now, focus on internal processes for updates, and learn Windows 10's functionality.

title: UC San Diego participates in Coursera Global Skills Initiative
summary: UC San Diego is participating in Coursera's Global Skills Initiative, a new program bringing universities and companies together to create "Specializations" in job-relevant skills. Two of the first three Specializations, focused on the Internet of Things and Big Data, are being produced by UC San Diego's Qualcomm Institute and San Diego Supercomputer Center respectively, with sponsorship from Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and Splunk. The initiative aims to address a global skills gap by providing high-quality, professionally-oriented online courses.

title: Indians hail Pichai’s rise to top Google job
summary: The Indian press and public have enthusiastically reacted to Sundar Pichai's appointment as Google's new CEO, seeing it as a source of national pride and highlighting his achievement as part of an elite group of Indian-origin individuals leading major global firms. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Pichai, whose story from humble beginnings in Chennai to the top of one of the world's most powerful internet companies has inspired many. Media outlets lauded Pichai's talent and managerial acumen, drawing parallels with other successful Indian-origin CEOs like Satya Nadella.

title: How Millennials Forced GE to Scrap Performance Reviews
summary: General Electric, a century-old company, is abandoning its traditional annual performance reviews and "rank and yank" system for its 300,000-strong workforce, moving to a new app-based system for more frequent feedback. This shift is partly driven by the expectations of millennials for more immediate and mobile-enabled feedback, and aligns with a broader restructuring of the company towards high-tech industrial businesses. The move by GE, which popularized rigid performance management, signifies a potential end for a long-standing corporate practice

title: Online Travel Agencies: Future Industry Outlook
summary: Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) have shown significant growth, driven by increasing leisure and business travel, with major players like Expedia, Priceline, and TripAdvisor generating substantial revenue. While developed markets like the US and Europe are mature, OTAs are focusing on newer markets and adapting to digital trends like mobile adoption and social media marketing to capture future growth. The article also hints at future threats to the OTA business model.

title: The most hyped emerging technology of 2015
summary: Gartner Inc.'s Hype Cycle of Emerging Technologies report identifies autonomous vehicles as the most hyped technology of 2015, alongside the Internet of Things. Despite significant media attention and technological advancements, Gartner warns of unrealistic expectations, stating that fully autonomous vehicles are still 5-10 years away from mainstream adoption due to cost, legal, and ethical challenges. The report predicts a phased approach to driverless cars and anticipates massive shifts in industries like auto sales when the technology matures.

title: SC asks search engines like Yahoo, Google to respond on sex determination Ads
summary: The Supreme Court of India has asked Google India, Yahoo India, and Microsoft Corporation to respond to allegations that they are violating a court order and Indian laws by not blocking advertisements related to sex determination of a foetus. This order followed a PIL petitioner's claim that search engines were still displaying such ads despite a previous court directive. The court is addressing the issue due to the decreasing number of girl children in the country.

title: Rackspace Is the Leader in the Hosted Private Cloud Market
summary: Rackspace leads the hosted private cloud market with a 20% market share, despite it being a highly fragmented market. While Amazon Web Services is the current leader in IaaS, Rackspace, Microsoft Azure, and VMware's vCloud Air are emerging as competitive challengers. A potential alliance between these three could significantly challenge Amazon's market dominance.

title: Foxconn boost for 'Make in India': Why Taiwan Inc's growing interests in India deserve attention
summary: Foxconn's renewed and significant investment in India, including a $5 billion electronics factory and R&D center in Maharashtra, signals a major boost for the "Make in India" campaign and the broader entry of Taiwanese companies into the Indian market. This move reflects Taiwan Inc's strategy to geographically de-risk from China, capitalize on India's large domestic market, and contribute to building a critical manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The article highlights the potential for increased Taiwanese investment beyond Foxconn, addressing India's need to reduce electronics imports and create jobs.

title: Maltese company Kinetix wins Microsoft’s IT Solutions Partner of the Year Award 2015
summary: Maltese IT service provider Kinetix Ltd has been awarded Microsoft's IT Solutions Partner of the Year Award 2015, announced at the Microsoft Worldwide Partner Conference in Orlando, Florida. This prestigious award recognizes Kinetix for its excellence in innovation and implementation of Microsoft's customer solutions and technology, distinguishing them among 2,300 entries from 108 countries. Kinetix, a Microsoft Gold Certified Partner since 2000, specializes in delivering ICT solutions for the corporate sector and is a local leader in providing IT solutions to top Maltese companies.

title: Driving the Connected Enterprise with intelligent technology
summary: This article discusses how intelligent technology, particularly the Internet of Things (IoT) and the "Intelligent Cloud" from Microsoft, is driving the "Connected Enterprise" and a fourth industrial revolution. Sanjay Ravi from Microsoft Corporation explains how manufacturers can leverage these technologies to transform business models, improve productivity, and make informed decisions, emphasizing the need for a digital mindset and strategic partnerships. The piece also addresses the importance of integrating existing expertise with new technologies and offers advice for SMEs on adopting these advancements.

title: Parsing The Biggest Tech Break Up Of All Time With HP CEO Meg Whitman
summary: Meg Whitman, CEO of HP, discusses the impending split of HP into two Fortune 50 companies, HP Inc. (PC and printers) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (enterprise products and services). She elaborates on the progress of the separation, the strategic rationale behind it, and her future role in both entities. Whitman also shares insights on technology valuations, the importance of diversity in tech, and lessons learned from her career, including her run for governor of California.

title: Caribbean Tech Trendz is Microsoft’s Local Partner of the Year
summary: Caribbean Tech Trendz Ltd (CTTL) has been awarded Microsoft Trinidad and Tobago Country Partner of the Year, recognizing its excellence in providing Microsoft products and services. The Gasparillo-based company was selected from over 2,300 global nominations for its strong services practice and as Microsoft's top cloud reach partner in 2015. CTTL CEO Donny Ramdathsingh received the award at the 2015 Microsoft Worldwide Partner Conference, validating the company's commitment to best-in-class solutions and customer service.

title: iPad envy prompted Microsoft Surface alliance
summary: Microsoft launched its Surface Enterprise Initiative with Dell and HP, among others, likely in response to Apple's business-focused iPad Pro. This initiative aims to push Windows 10-based tablets into corporate accounts, a market where Apple devices have already made significant inroads. Despite internal conflicts and their own hardware offerings, HP and Dell's participation highlights a collective concern among these companies regarding Apple's dominance

title: Drugs Found Stashed on Teekay LNG Carrier in Peru
summary: The Peruvian Navy confiscated over 200 kilograms of cocaine found on a Teekay LNG carrier, Hispania Spirit, anchored near Pisco, Peru. The drugs were stashed near the vessel's rudder, a common tactic for smugglers, and a Venezuelan national not part of the crew was also found. The ship, owned by Teekay Corporation, was destined for Manzanillo, Mexico.

title: HP Enterprise: Can it overcome layoffs, split growing pains, and FUD?
summary: HP Enterprise is undergoing a major transformation, splitting from Hewlett-Packard, cutting 25,000 to 30,000 jobs, and focusing on private and hybrid cloud with a goal of $3 billion in annual cloud revenue in 2015. The company faces the challenge of convincing enterprise buyers amidst potential "fear, uncertainty, and doubt" (FUD) from rivals, despite Meg Whitman's plan for a more focused and profitable entity. The main questions revolve around its ability to innovate and provide stability during this significant restructure.

title: The real reason for HP’s woes (and no, it’s not Autonomy)
summary: This article argues that HP's 2008 acquisition of Electronic Data Systems (EDS) for $13.9 billion was a more significant contributor to the company's long-term struggles than the widely criticized 2011 Autonomy purchase. The EDS deal led to an $8 billion write-down and the current challenges faced by HP Enterprise Services, necessitating layoffs and offshoring. While CEO Meg Whitman highlights hybrid cloud growth, HP has fallen out of the public cloud leadership, indicating continued difficulties in the evolving IT landscape.

title: Microsoft announces three new console bundles to celebrates first anniversary of Xbox One
summary: Microsoft is celebrating the first anniversary of the Xbox One by introducing three new console bundles. These bundles include a Forza Motorsport 6 Limited Edition console, a 1TB EA Sports FIFA 16 bundle, and an Xbox One Gears of War: Ultimate Edition bundle, offering different games and storage options to cater to various gamers. The bundles are launching on October 2nd, with pre-orders available on Amazon.in.

title: SkyWest, Inc. chooses Surface and Windows 10 over iPad for 7,500 pilots
summary: SkyWest, Inc. is deploying Surface 3 devices running Windows 10 Professional to 7,500 pilots across its ExpressJet Airlines and SkyWest Airlines subsidiaries, replacing heavy paper-based flight kits. The decision was driven by the security and management capabilities of Windows 10 on Surface 3, demonstrating a growing trend of commercial airlines adopting Surface tablets for Electronic Flight Bags (EFBs). Surface 3 has also been pre-qualified for FAA and EASA authorization, streamlining the deployment process for airlines.

title: Jeff Kilburg
summary: Jeff Kilburg is the Founder, CEO, and CIO of KKM Financial, an asset management company in Chicago, IL. KKM Financial offers various services including outsourced CIO services, model portfolios, and market commentary globally. Kilburg also serves as a portfolio manager for the Essential 40 Stock ETF (ESN) and contributes market insights and options trading strategies to CNBC.

title: Nelson Peltz's Trian takes $2.5 billion stake in General Electric
summary: Activist investor Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has acquired a $2.5 billion stake in General Electric, making it a top-10 shareholder and adding pressure for the conglomerate to accelerate its shift towards industrial operations. Trian aims for cost cutting, more share buybacks, and further scaling back of GE Capital, backing GE's ongoing transformation. General Electric's shares rose 4.5% following the disclosure, with Trian projecting its stock could reach $40-$45 per share by the end of 2017.

title: The 12 biggest technology acquisitions of all time
summary: This article details the 12 largest technology acquisitions of all time as of October 2015, highlighting Dell's record-breaking $67 billion agreement to acquire EMC. It outlines significant deals such as Avago's purchase of Broadcom and Facebook's acquisition of WhatsApp, providing financial figures and context for each. The article also touches on the strategic reasons behind these mergers, particularly Dell's move into data storage amid declining PC sales.

title: Microsoft Surface Book’s Nvidia GPU is decent, but it’s no gaming laptop
summary: Microsoft's Surface Book features a dedicated Nvidia GPU, which new reports suggest is equivalent to the mid-range GeForce 940M. While this makes the Surface Book capable for average laptop use and some gaming at lower settings, it is not competitive with dedicated gaming laptops due to its focus on portability and battery life. The Surface Book does, however, hold an advantage over the Macbook Pro in gaming thanks to its Windows operating system and a broader game library.

title: Microsoft nominates Johnson & Johnson’s Sandra Peterson, ex-Cisco Systems executive Padmasree Warrior to board
summary: Microsoft has nominated Johnson & Johnson's Sandra Peterson and former Cisco Systems executive Padmasree Warrior to its board, aiming to increase diversity. These additions would bring the board's total to 11 members, including three women, following Maria Klawe's decision not to seek re-election. The article also details CEO Satya Nadella's and CFO Amy Hood's compensation for fiscal 2015, which saw a drop for Nadella compared to the previous year.

title: Zscaler Leader in the SaaS Web Content Security Market
summary: Zscaler has been recognized as a Leader in the SaaS Web Content Security market by Forrester Research, Inc. in its Q2 2015 report. The report highlights Zscaler's top scores in Current Offering, Strategy, and Market Presence, and notes the industry shift from on-premises web gateways to the SaaS model. Zscaler's CEO, Jay Chaudhry, emphasizes the validation of their cloud-based security platform as essential for businesses.

title: Nasdaq may see record with Apple earnings
summary: The Nasdaq 100 index, heavily influenced by US technology stocks such as Apple, is poised to potentially set a new record high, driven by strong earnings anticipated from Apple Inc. Technology shares have led the market's recovery, with gains in Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft following better-than-expected earnings. Despite being an "underperformer" among tech giants recently, Apple's expected revenue increase and positive market sentiment suggest its upcoming earnings report could push the Nasdaq 100 to a record.

title: Macroeconomic Factors Affecting Microsoft’s Performance
summary: This article discusses the macroeconomic factors affecting Microsoft's performance, primarily focusing on competition in the technology sector and the company's strategic focus on cloud business. It highlights Microsoft's major competitors in the cloud segment, including Amazon, IBM, and Google, and outlines Microsoft's strategy to succeed in the mobile-first and cloud-first space, detailing the resources and focus areas required for growth. The article also provides financial details, noting Microsoft's revenue increase in 1Q16 and its representation in key tech ETFs.

title: Bye-bye HP, Hello HP Enterprise and HP Inc.
summary: On Sunday, Hewlett-Packard will split into two publicly traded companies: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and HP Inc. This move follows a history of strategic missteps and controversial acquisitions for the tech giant, which started in 1939. The split aims to create more focused businesses, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise handling servers, software, storage, networking, and services, while HP Inc. will focus on printers and PCs.

title: Hewlett-Packard Splits in Two Today. Now What?
summary: Hewlett-Packard officially split into two separate companies. HP Inc. focuses on PCs and printing, while Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE) handles servers, networking, and software, with CEO Meg Whitman leading the latter. This move aims to make both entities more agile in a changing tech market, with HPE planning potential acquisitions despite facing challenges from cloud computing rivals.

title: Hewlett-Packard becomes HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise
summary: Hewlett-Packard officially split into two publicly listed companies, HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), on November 2, 2015. HP Inc. will focus on PCs and printers, while HPE will concentrate on commercial computer systems, software, and tech services. This split, planned since the previous year, aims to make the new entities more agile and responsive to their respective market segments.

title: Amazon opens a physical bookstore, but still hopes you buy online
summary: Amazon opened its first physical bookstore, Amazon Books, in Seattle, 15 years after starting as an online bookseller. The store aims to be a physical extension of Amazon.com, allowing customers to try out Amazon devices and browse books displayed with online customer ratings. Prices in the store match online prices, and customers are encouraged to browse in-store but buy online.

title: Microsoft To Stop Sale of Windows 7&8
summary: Microsoft has given its PC partners a one-year ultimatum to sell computers running Windows 7 or Windows 8.1, with sales ending October 31, 2016, to push adoption of Windows 10. The end-of-sales date for Windows 8 is even earlier, June 30, 2016, due to poor demand. Users with genuine Windows 7 or 8 copies can upgrade to Windows 10 for free, as Windows 7 still dominates the market despite Windows 10's growing presence.

title: Auto, tech companies pledge $4.5 million to Focus: HOPE
summary: Five automotive and technology companies have pledged nearly $4.5 million to Focus: HOPE’s workforce and development programs. These pledges are a first step toward the organization's goal of securing $30 million in private funding over the next five years to sustain critical education and workforce development initiatives. The contributing companies include Microsoft Corp., Magna International, Lear Corp., the GM Foundation, and Ford Motor Company.

title: HPE 3Par makes the move to all-flash data centre
summary: HPE's 3Par unit released a new series of StoreServ Storage products to drive the adoption of all-flash data centers. This move comes as IDC highlights the undeniable impact of flash-based arrays, and HPE positions these products for IT-as-a-Service and data analytics trends. The company also integrated 3Par StoreServ with StoreOnce and StoreEver, offering various new products and upgrades at competitive price points.

title: Canadian Pacific CEO Hunter Harrison Hunts for His Biggest M&A Deal
summary: Canadian Pacific CEO Hunter Harrison is exploring a takeover of Norfolk Southern Corp., aiming to create a transcontinental carrier. This potential deal would be his most ambitious merger, testing his reputation for efficiency and deal-making. Despite his track record of turning railroads around, the sheer size of the acquisition and potential regulatory and union hurdles would present significant challenges.

title: 10 years of achievement – Microsoft at the top of the Corporate Equality Index again
summary: Microsoft has achieved a perfect score on the Corporate Equality Index (CEI) for the tenth consecutive year, highlighting its ongoing commitment to LGBT workplace inclusion. The company has a long history of supporting LGBT rights, including offering same-sex domestic partnership benefits since 1993 and actively advocating for same-sex marriage. The article emphasizes that senior leadership and employee advocacy are crucial to fostering an inclusive environment and addressing global challenges in LGBT equality.

title: The HP Elite x2: Stunning, Secure, and Built for Business
summary: HP Inc. announced the HP Elite x2, a versatile tablet designed for mobile professionals, offering both the productivity of a notebook and the convenience of a tablet. It features BIOS-level security, manageability with HP Touchpoint Manager, and optional Intel vPro processor, making it a secure and powerful device for business. The Elite x2 will start shipping in January 2016 in the United States, with pre-orders beginning November 23rd at a starting price of $899, including the HP Travel Keyboard and HP Active Pen.

title: Hewlett Packard’s Spawn Get Off to a Slow Start
summary: Hewlett Packard's final earnings report as a combined entity revealed declining revenue, prompting its split into two companies: HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Both new companies provided financial forecasts below analyst expectations, attributing the shortfall to unfavorable exchange rates and a tough market. While HP Inc. faced challenges with printer sales to consumers affecting ink revenue, HPE showed some promise with increased server sales and a new partnership with Microsoft.

title: UNESCO, Microsoft, True Corp and Thailand’s Office of Non-Formal and Informal Education launch ICT education project to empower learners at Thai-Myanmar border
summary: UNESCO, Microsoft, True Corp, and the Thai Ministry of Education’s Office of Non-Formal and Informal Education (ONIE) launched the "Mobile Literacy for Out-of-School Children Project" to provide learning opportunities and educational resources to disadvantaged young learners along the Thai-Myanmar border. This initiative involves distributing Windows tablets pre-loaded with a UNESCO-designed app, providing internet and digital media from True Corp, and offering training and materials from ONIE, aiming to empower 4,000 learners and 100 teachers. The project aligns with global sustainable development goals to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education through the integration of ICT.

title: HPE Discover 2015 keynote focuses on Synergy and four areas of enterprise transformation | #HPEDiscover
summary: The HPE Discover 2015 conference focused on the company's corporate shift and future plans, particularly after its separation into HP, Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. The keynote highlighted four areas of enterprise transformation: hybrid infrastructure, protection, enabling productivity, and empowering data-driven organizations. A major announcement was HPE Synergy, a technology designed to optimize infrastructure for both traditional and new "idea economy" workloads.

title: BackStab: Mobile Backup Data Under Attack from Malware
summary: A whitepaper reveals that malware is stealing private mobile device data by accessing local backup files stored on PCs and Macs, a technique dubbed "BackStab." This attack has been observed globally for over five years, affecting iOS and BlackBerry devices by exploiting unencrypted backup files. Users are advised to encrypt backups, use strong passwords, update their OS, and be cautious when connecting devices to untrusted computers to mitigate this threat.

title: Google and NASA Show Off Quantum Computing Machine
summary: Google and NASA showcased their experimental quantum super-computing system, a D-Wave 2X machine, which is being used to solve complex problems faster than conventional computers. Researchers emphasized that quantum computing is still in its experimental stages, akin to early conventional computers, and is not yet a commercial product, though companies like IBM, Intel, and Microsoft are also researching the technology. Despite some scientific debate about whether the D-Wave machine is a "true" quantum computer, Google and NASA are studying its capabilities, with Google having published findings on its speed advantages for certain calculations.

title: Stock buybacks enrich executive pay even when business sags
summary: This article examines how stock buybacks can artificially inflate earnings per share (EPS), leading to higher executive compensation even when a company's underlying business performance is weak. It highlights specific cases, such as Humana Inc., Xerox Corp., and Activision Blizzard, where buybacks helped executives meet performance targets and receive substantial bonuses. The piece also discusses broader criticisms that these practices prioritize short-term gains and executive enrichment over long-term corporate health and investment.

title: Microsoft’s Cortana comes to Android, iOS devices in US and China
summary: Microsoft has rolled out its voice-assistant Cortana for select iPhone and Android devices, as well as Cyanogen OS-powered devices, in the US and China. Cortana, a rival to Google Now and Apple's Siri, will allow Windows PC users to connect their mobile devices to their PCs and offer features like setting reminders and tracking flights, with changes syncing across all devices. While some Windows Phone features like hands-free activation or toggling settings won't be available on Android and iOS, Cyanogen devices will have a more integrated experience allowing "Hey Cortana" activation and control over network modes and Quiet Mode.

title: India has to wait for low-cost Windows 10 phones: Microsoft exec
summary: Microsoft executive Steve Guggenheimer stated that India will have to wait for low-cost Windows 10 Lumia smartphones as the company focuses on rebranding and launching new generation, higher-end devices first. He indicated that the company aims to scale the Lumia line to other price points over time, explaining that the current focus is on competing with companies like Apple in the high-margin segment. Microsoft has already launched its high-end Lumia 950 and 950 XL in India, both running Windows 10.

title: Indian IT: From outsourced computer services to global business partners
summary: The Indian IT sector has transformed from providing outsourced services to becoming global business partners, exemplified by Infosys's strategic technology partnership with the ATP. This evolution, marked by significant growth and job creation, is also facing challenges like infrastructure issues and talent quality, prompting the industry and government to adapt and invest in education and new business models focused on software development and technology-based solutions. The article highlights India's emergence as a dominant player in the global IT industry, moving beyond simple outsourcing to becoming a partner in progress for clients worldwide.

title: $8 billion NetApp is buying a storage company for $870 million in cash
summary: NetApp, a storage tech giant with an $8 billion market cap, is acquiring SolidFire, a solid-state storage startup, for $870 million in an all-cash deal. This acquisition will help NetApp enhance its appeal to large enterprises that are seeking more efficient and scalable data center solutions. SolidFire specializes in creating storage systems for enterprise data centers that utilize solid-state flash drives, offering a faster and more energy-efficient alternative to traditional hard drives.

title: Microsoft will participate in Indian startup growth story: Nadella
summary: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft, announced the company's participation in accelerating the Indian startup ecosystem during his visit to Hyderabad. He visited T-Hub, an incubation facility, and discussed partnerships with the Telangana and Andhra Pradesh governments for technology support in various sectors. Nadella also addressed budding entrepreneurs, emphasizing the importance of concept, capability, and culture in startup development.

title: Apple iPhone 7 OLED display to be supplied by LG, Samsung: report
summary: LG Display Co Ltd and Samsung Electronics' panel-making unit are reportedly set to supply OLED screens for Apple Inc's iPhones, starting with the iPhone 7. This move follows years of speculation about Apple adopting next-generation display technology, with the Korean firms planning significant capital expenditure to boost OLED production capacity. Apple may also provide funding to assist with these investments.
